sections.content: How many people are "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations"?

9,765 people

were counted on the census as "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations mark off, drill, shape, position, rivet and seal metal plates and girders to form structures and frameworks, operate power hammers and presses to shape heated metal to requirements, make and repair a variety of metal articles, make moulds and cores for casting metal, and pour or inject molten metal into dies.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations" there were more men than women (95% compared with 5%).

This means "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 95% and women made up 5% of "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations" included:

  • TV, video and audio servicers and repairers
  • electrical engineers
  • window cleaners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations", 13.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

We can look at who worked as "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations", 9.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.5% compared with 13.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (66.3%) than self-employed (33.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was Yorkshire and the Humber. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Rotherham, this is in the same region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
